tossups.text: Philip José Farmer wrote his biography Venus on the Half-shell. In a 1987 interview, his creator admitted that he was inspired by the science fiction writer Theodore Sturgeon. Mentioned in Jailbird, his son Leon narrates Galapagos while he himself makes his first appearance in God Bless You, Mr. Rosewater. For 10 points, who is this creation of Kurt Vonnegut, the main character of Timequake and Breakfast of Champions?

After his family was expelled from Portugal, this city became the home of rabbi Menasseh ben Israel, who later negotiated with Oliver Cromwell to allow Jews to reside in England. The high prices fetched by items such as the Semper Augustus in this capital city are described in an exaggerated account by Charles MacKay. In 1603, the world's first stock exchange was founded in this city by the world's first multinational corporation, which was known by the initials VOC. Tulip bulbs were traded on that stock exchange in this capital city during a 17th-century mania. In 1656, its Jewish community expelled the young philosopher Baruch Spinoza. For 10 points, concentric rings of canals surround what capital of the Netherlands?

The Hicksian function of this quantity maximizes a consumer's expenditure over fixed utility. Marketing, Sales, and Service are constituent parts of this quantity's "chain." Price elasticity measures this quantity responsiveness to changes in price. Giffen goods are an exception to this quantity's "law," which states that as prices drop, this quantity increases. For 10 points, name this economic measurement of willingness of consumers to pay for a good, often paired with supply.

In human physiology, this structure is essential for vaccines and immunization. It plays a key role in the immune system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this vaccine-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The vaccine is a key component of the Immune system, involved in vaccines and immunization.

tossups.text: In one paper, this philosopher cites Kierkegaard's essay "The Present Age," which argues that anonymity undermines commitment, to demonstrate why "Kierkegaard would have hated the Internet." Another of this philosopher's papers draws parallels between two philosophers' use of the title concepts, and is titled "Being and Power." With Paul Rabinow, this thinker authored a book entitled Michel Foucault: Beyond Structuralism and Hermeneutics, and in 1997, he engaged in a notable debate with Daniel Dennett regarding the recent match between Kasparov and Deep Blue. In addition to writing a popular exposition of Heidegger's Being and Time entitled Being-in-the-world, this thinker wrote a work which critiqued the biological, psychological, epistemological, and ontological assumptions "underlying persistent optimism," and argues for the "role of the body in intelligent behavior." For 10 points, identify this phenomenologist and Heidegger exponent, a Berkeley philosopher whose criticism against artificial intelligence is contained in What Computers Still Can't Do.

This man wrote a 1729 satirical essay suggesting that poor people in Ireland should sell their children as food. The protagonist in one of his novels goes to the flying island of Laputa. That character also goes to a land of giants called Brobdingnag and a land of very small people called Lilliput. For 10 points, name this author of A Modest Proposal and Gulliver's Travels.

A chapter of this novel alternates each sentence between passages from Benito Pérez Galdós's novel The Prohibited and the protagonist's thoughts while reading it. A character in this novel removes washbasins from a clinic, puts them in his room, and sews together his belongings with string to ward off his "doppelgänger." A part of this novel ends with "three garish little stars," which "stand for the words The End." In this novel, Gregorovius woos a woman who vanishes after her baby Rocamadour passes away, after which the protagonist begins working at a circus with Talita and Traveler. This novel's section "From Diverse Sides" includes the author Morelli's notes among its 99 "expendable chapters." A table of instructions details multiple ways of reading, for 10 points, what novel by Julio Cortázar?

A method of sample preparation for this technique, in which a vacuum chamber is heated to create infrared radiation and trigger photodissociation, is called BIRD. Aberrant acylcarnitine ("ass-ill-CARN-uh-teen") profiles determined from this technique can be used to diagnose a deficiency of medium-chain acyl-coenzyme A dehydrogenase in newborns. When subject to this technique, benzyl groups frequently rearrange to form the tropylium cation. Samples with chlorine form two peaks whose heights have a ratio of 3-to-1 in this technique, because of the different abundances of its isotopes. This technique is used "in tandem" for protein sequencing. For 10 points, name this technique that separates atoms and molecules by molecular weight.

This leader used the Falk Laws to combat Pius IX's influence in his nation, while the Battle of Sedan occurred in a war that this man started by editing the Ems Dispatch. This initiator of the Kulturkampf against the Catholic Chuch hosted the Congress of Berlin and united his nation through the Franco-Prussian War. While advising Wilhelm I, this man practiced Realpolitik. For 10 points, name this Prussian, the Iron Chancellor of Germany.

The intrinsically-conducting type of these substances is used in OLEDs. In these substances, the glass transition temperature measures the point at which parts of it start sliding past one another, and differential scanning calorimetry is often used to find that temperature. In structural formulas, these are written with a segment in parentheses and a subscript "n", and they can be described as chain-growth or step-growth. Ones that can be remolded upon heating, like PVC, are called thermoplastic. One biological one that is produced by a branching enzyme is starch. For 10 points, name these compounds that are made of repeating structural units called monomers.

In human anatomy, this structure is essential for spinal nerves. It plays a key role in the nervous system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this spinal cord-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The spinal cord is a key component of the Nervous system, involved in spinal nerves.

tossups.text: The family that contains this protein also contains a protein suspected to soften the pubis symphysis, which peaks during the first trimester of pregnancy and at delivery. Regulatory sequences of the gene that codes for this protein include MafA and the CAAT enhancer binding element, and NeuroD1 regulates its synthesis. The release of this hormone occurs in a three- to six-minute rhythm, and HGH induces the liver to secrete one of a family of growth factors with sequence similarity to it. This hormone is released following IP3 binding to the ER, triggering calcium release. For 10 points, name this hormone, secreted by the beta cells in the pancreas, which induces tissues to take up glucose and is administered to sufferers of diabetes.

In a series depicting his studio, this artist paid tribute to Henri Matisse's L'Atelier Rouge in a painting that shows a figure who, in a different work, gazes at this artist's initials in the water. Many of his subjects are women in relationships with domineering men, such as the blonde women in Hopeless and Crying Girl. This artist showed a character who's snagged his rod while exclaiming "I've hooked a big one!" in an example of his use of Ben-Day dots. For 10 points, identify this Pop artist of Look, Mickey! and Whaam!

This instrument was played by the composers of Blood on the Fields and "A Night in Tunisia," who played a bent one of these instruments. This instrument was played by a musician who included "Flamenco Sketches" and "Freddie Freeloader" on his album Kind of Blue, and by Wynton Marsalis and Dizzy Gillespie. Louis Armstrong was nicknamed "Satchmo" for playing this instrument with puffed cheeks. For 10 points, name this three-valved brass instrument played by Miles Davis.

This quantity is equal to the sum of the pKa ["P-K-A"] value and the logarithm of a ratio of concentrations according to the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation. Titrations commonly use phenolphthalein ["fee"-nol-THAY-leen] as an indicator to detect a change in this quantity. Substances that are used to resist the change of this quantity are known as buffers. This value for pure water at 25° C ["25 degrees C"] is 7, meaning that it is neutral. For ten points, name this relative scale that determines how acidic or basic a substance is.

This quantity is zero for a Majorana fermion. Surface integrating the electric field gives this quantity. The change in this quantity due to friction is described by the triboelectric effect. A ratio of mass to this quantity is important in mass spectrometers. This quantity was shown to be quantized by the Millikan oil drop experiment. Condensers and Leyden jars were used to store this quantity. The movement of this quantity is quantified by its time derivative, current. For 10 points, name this quantity, symbolized q and measured in Coulombs, which is negative for an electron.

Jane Fulcher's book The Nation as Art rejects the traditional thesis that this style rose in prominence due to the influence of Louis Véron. In a composition in this style, deceased women rise from their tombs to seduce a knight in the "Ballet of the Nuns." The prayer "Nume del Ciel" ("NOO-may del CHELL") is sung before battle in another composition in this style that ends with an eruption of Mount Vesuvius. In a third composition in this style, the ringing of a bell signals the beginning of a massacre, after which Raoul jumps out a window. Canonically, the earliest work in this style is Daniel Auber's ("don-YELL oh-BAY's") The Mute Girl of Portici. Works in this style include Hector Berlioz's Les Troyens ("lay twah-YANN") and most of the output of Giacomo Meyerbeer ("JAH-ko-mo MY-er-beer"). For 10 points, name this dominant style of opera in early 19th-century France characterized by lavish designs and very large orchestras.

This man took the name "Black Raven" while living with one tribe. This man's forces won a battle with the help of a pair of cannons known as the "Twin Sisters." This man's request for federal rations for Native Americans led to an affair in which he beat Ohio Representative William Stanbery with a cane. Edward Clark succeeded this man as governor after he refused to secede to the Confederacy. This man's popularity surged after his victory at the Battle of San Jacinto, allowing him to defeat Stephen Austin in an 1836 election. For 10 points, name this two-term president of the Republic of Texas who names its most populous city.

The cords of Billroth are near its sinusoid vessels and it also contains the linear hilum. Gaucher's disease can affect this organ, which contains the Malphigian corpuscles and is connected to the lienal artery by the reticulum. Composed of red and white pulp, its functions include the creation of red blood cells before birth and lymphocyte production throughout life. For 10 points, identify this organ located to the left of the stomach and below the diaphragm, which also destroys red blood cells.

One culture that lived in this modern-day country were known as the Warriors of the Clouds, who built a walled-city named Kuelap. A common figure in the ancient mythology of this country was the mysterious "Staff God" who was depicted by multiple cultures. The oldest city in the Americas was founded in this modern-day country in around 3500 BC. That city was Huaricanga. One culture that lived in this modern-day country drew large geoglyphs of animals like monkeys and hummingbirds that can only be seen from the air. That culture was the Nazca. For 10 points, name this country, whose city of Cuzco was also the capital of the Incan Empire.

parts.text: Name this play, which opens with an Englishman seated by an English fire while the English clock strikes 17 English strokes. In this absurdist play, the Fire Chief interrupts a dinner between the Martins and the Smiths.
In The Bald Soprano, Mary declares that she is this fictional detective. This character, created by Arthur Conan Doyle, works with Dr. John Watson.
The Bald Soprano was written by this Romanian-French absurdist playwright, who also described Berenger's refusal to turn into the title animal in the play Rhinoceros.

bonuses.leadin: In this play, the maid Mary reads a poem about the water, sky, and ashes all catching on fire. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this agency that regulates air waves and TV broadcasts.
This FCC rule required stations to present multiple viewpoints when discussing controversial issues. Unlike the equal-time rule, this doctrine was abolished in 1987.

One of the inaugural FCC commissioners, Norman Case, also served as governor of this state. Longtime senators from this state include Theodore F. Green and Claiborne Pell, the namesake of the Pell Grant.

bonuses.leadin: The 1934 act that established this agency replaced a similar agency created by the Radio Act of 1927. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this rejected time period that would have followed the Holocene, which began about twelve thousandyears ago. This name reflects humanity's impact on the Earth.

The rejection was due to disagreement over the start date of the Anthropocene, with some scientistspreferring this "revolution" twelve thousand years ago as the marker. This term, which translates as "New Stone,"describes the age in which farming, animal domestication, and permanent settlements developed.
Arguments for marking the Anthropocene include mankind's contribution to climate change and to thisnatural process, in which all members of a species die off.

bonuses.leadin: In March 2024, the International Union of Geological Sciences voted down a proposal to update thegeologic time scale with a new epoch beginning in roughly 1950. For ten points each,

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with red blood cells and hemoglobin.
What is the main function of the erythrocyte in the cardiovascular system?
Name another component of the cardiovascular system related to red blood cells and hemoglobin.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human cardiovascular system.

parts.text: Name this philosopher who espoused a philosophy of optimism in Discourses in Verse on Man.

In 1764, Voltaire argued that the Judeo-Christian conception of God was false, but that there was an impersonal deity in a "Philosophical" work of this type; one year later, Voltaire released an edition of that book that was meant "for the Pocket."
Voltaire's Dictionary thus espoused this viewpoint that there is a God who does not intervene in the universe. Thomas Jefferson also espoused this view.

bonuses.leadin: This philosopher had to flee from Paris for yet a third time after he praised the practice of inoculation and attacked French religion in his book Philosophical Letters. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Roman poet who is best known for his narrative poem Metamorphoses.
Another Roman poet, Horace, wrote many of these poems. Friedrich Schiller wrote one of these poems "to Joy" which was set to music by Beethoven.
Ovid and Horace wrote in this language which was spoken in the Roman Empire. This language's phrase "carpe diem" roughly translates as "seize the day".

bonuses.leadin: This poet wrote the Ars Amatoria, or The Art of Love. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this play in which Edward is shocked to discover that his psychiatrist Dr. Henry Harcourt-Reilly is the same mysterious guest whom he had confided in about his wife's disappearance.
T. S. Eliot's play The Cocktail Party parodied a genre of Victorian comedy of manners named for the fact that they were typically set in this type of place.

This author wrote a drawing-room comedy about the Bliss family titled Hay Fever. After a séance ("SAY-once"), Charles Condomime is haunted by the ghost of his annoying first wife in his play Blithe Spirit.

bonuses.leadin: In this play's opening scene, a character is asked to tell the story of Lady Klootz and the wedding cake, but instead distractedly gossips about Delia Verinder's brother, who can hear bats. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Give this technology, which is typically implemented with the IEEE 802.11 standard. Devices using this technology often use the 2.4 or 5 gigahertz frequencies.

Wi-Fi relies on these entities to ensure proper communication at the physical layer. Defined in the network interface controller of devices like modems, an ARP table associates these entities with IP addresses.
MAC ("mack") addresses consist of 6 pairs of digits in this numerical system. For example, the MAC address used to broadcast a message to every computer on a network would have 12 F's.

bonuses.leadin: In an ad hoc paradigm, devices can communicate with each other via this technology without an intermediary. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this woman who survived an assassination attempt by Jared Lee Loughner in 2011.
In 2012, another widely publicized shooting occurred when George Zimmerman shot this high school student wearing a hoodie and carrying Skittles.
This Norwegian terrorist set off a car bomb in Oslo and carried out a mass shooting in Utoya, which he claimed to do in order to fight against the forces of Islam and multiculturalism.

bonuses.leadin: Her husband, Mark Kelly, is a NASA astronaut, and she is one of Arizona's Representatives. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this molecule that is transported in the bloodstream by the lipoproteins HDL and LDL, often known as its "good" and "bad" varieties.
This vitamin is synthesized in humans when the cholesterol derivative 7-DHC has a ring broken by ultraviolet rays. This fat-soluble vitamin is required to absorb calcium from food.
acceptableAnswers: their chemical names such as cholecalciferol

parts.text: This hormone derived from cholesterol is a precursor to all other sex hormones. Mifepristone is an antagonist of this hormone which, along with estrogens, is used in contraceptives and hormone replacement therapy.

bonuses.leadin: This molecule is produced by animals to maintain fluidity in cell membranes. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with synaptic transmission.
What is the main function of the axon in the nervous system?
Name another component of the nervous system related to synaptic transmission.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human nervous system.

parts.text: Name these organomagnesium halide reagents.
The reaction of Grignard reagents with nitriles yields ketones. The simplest nitrile is this moiety, with formula CN minus, which smells of almonds when bound to hydrogen.

Among others, this nonpolar aprotic solvent is commonly used when reacting alkyl halides and magnesium under anhydrous conditions to form Grignard reagents. The main structural unit of this solvent is a heterocyclic five-membered ring with four carbon atoms and one oxygen atom.

bonuses.leadin: These reagents exist as an equilibrium of several different organometallic compounds called the Schlenk equilibrium. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This Ukrainian born ballet dancer dramatically resigned from the Royal Ballet in 2012, just two years after he had become the company's youngest ever principal.
Among Polunin's many accolades is a 2006 gold medal from this Swiss competition for young dancers, whose top prize has previously been won by Darcey Bussell and Carlos Acosta.
Polunin's extensive repertoire at the Royal Ballet included originating the role of the Knave of Hearts in this work based on a children's novel, choreographed by Christopher Wheeldon.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer the following questions relating to a dancer.

parts.text: A short piece by Rimsky-Korsakov features runs of sixteenth notes on violin or flute to depict the "Flight of" this stinging insect.

Rimsky-Korsakov depicted the legendary Russian musician Sadko in an 1867 work in this genre of one-movement compositions that illustrate a story. Richard Strauss' Also Sprach Zarathustra is another of these works.
The movements of this other Rimsky-Korsakov symphonic poem depict stories from The Arabian Nights and are separated by solo violin intermezzos signifying the title character, the wife of Shahriyar.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, give the following about Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov.

parts.text: Adding all of the values in a set, then dividing by the total number of values, gives you the arithmetic type of this statistic.
In geometry, this point is the average location of all the points in a two-dimensional shape. If the shape has uniform density, this point is also the center of mass.
In probability, the long-term average outcome of an experiment is called this. For example, this quantity for "rolling a fair six-sided die once" is three point five.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, name the following mathematical measurements that take into account the "weight" of the values.

parts.text: Name this protein that, along with neurofibrillary tangles, can lead to a form of dementia by forming plaques.
Formation of beta-amyloid plaques in neurons is a characteristic sign of this neurodegenerative disease that causes memory loss.
Asao Hirano discovered that aggregations of this protein in neurons also play a role in the development of Alzheimer's disease. Microfilaments of this protein help comprise the cytoskeleton of cells.

bonuses.leadin: This molecule's namesake precursor protein functions as a cell surface receptor for neurons. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this National Park in the Sierra Nevada where Ansel Adams took photos such as El Capitan and Moon over Half Dome.

Adams photographed the Sierra's second-highest peak, Mount Williamson, while taking photos of this facility for the book Born Free and Equal. Adams created a series depicting women's calisthenics at this facility.

In 1942, this photographer also took photos of Mount Williamson overlooking Manzanar. This photographer, who was later employed by the FSA, documented the Depression era in images such as White Angel Breadline.

bonuses.leadin: A series of "Parmelian Prints" of this location inspired the Zone System with the dark, red-filtered photo Monolith. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this military unit that would signal a rebellion by overturning a sacred cauldron. This unit was once filled from the devşirme system.
In a bid to thwart Janissary plots in 1662, the Ottoman sultan tried to close namesake "houses" serving this hot, caffeinated beverage.

Osman II, who feuded with his Janissaries, ruled over one of these natural disasters in 1621 that caused widespread famine. One of these disasters contributed to a period of hunger in the Netherlands in the last year of World War II.
acceptableAnswers: accept anything involving an extended cold period

bonuses.leadin: The number of these people swelled to over 400,000 after changes in the 17th century allowed them to marry and run businesses. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these biochemical messengers with effects outside their area of production within an organism's body.
Production of this hormone in the pineal gland is inhibited by light. It helps induce drowsiness and regulate body temperature.
Melatonin is a key hormone in this 24-hour physiological cycle, whose sleep / wake aspect adjusts with the current time regardless an organism's location.

bonuses.leadin: Notable steroid examples include testosterone and estrogen. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this river that rises in the Tibetan Plateau and flows into the Andaman Sea at Mawlamyine [maw-LAWM-yeen], east of the Irrawaddy Delta. This river, along with the Yangtze and Mekong make up the Three Parallel Rivers.

The Three Parallel Rivers can be found within this southwest Chinese province home to the scenic Tiger Leaping Gorge. This province's capital is Kunming [kwun-meeng], and it lies south of Sichuan [suh-chwuhn].
The Salween River travels along the border between this country and its eastern neighbor, Thailand. Many of this country's Rohingya [row-HIN-juh] people have fled west into Bangladesh.
acceptableAnswers: Republic of the Union of Myanmar

bonuses.leadin: This river is known as the nujiang [noo-jee-ahng] in China. For 10 points each:
